title: Mission Control
tagline: Your induction. Your codename. Your first badges.
objectives: I can log in to my C2k account, find my way around the DT platform, and locate my saved work.
I can explain what locked and unlocked lessons mean and where to go if I get stuck.
I know at least one way to keep my account safe and what happens to files saved in the wrong place.

config.headline: You have been recruited.
lines: Our Lady's needs a new generation of Digital Agents.
Your mission spans one year: seventeen operations across Your Digital World.
Machines. Code. Networks. Design. You will master all of them.
This is Mission Control. Every operation you complete unlocks the next badge in your Agent File.

config.intro: Three warm-up pings to calibrate your Agent console. These are practice taps — nothing is scored. Tap what you think, see what happens.

items.stem: Which of these is the STRONGEST password?
What does a padlock on a lesson tile mean?
options: It isn't unlocked yet — your teacher opens it

items.stem: Where should your DT work live so it follows you to any computer?

config.intro: Every agent must get into HQ unaided. Prove you can handle your C2k identity — then lock in the ground rules.

steps.title: Find your credential slip
steps.text: Your teacher has given you a slip with your C2k username. It looks like: jbloggs123. Your username plus @c2ken.net is your school identity — it works on EVERY school computer.
steps.confirm: I can see my username on my slip

steps.title: Type your username — practice run
steps.text: Type your username into the practice console below, exactly as it appears on your slip. Watch for sneaky spaces and Caps Lock!

steps.title: Your password stays YOURS
steps.text: Your password is the one thing you never type where anyone can see, never share — not even with your best friend — and never save in a file. If you think someone knows it, tell a teacher and change it.
steps.confirm: I understand my password is only for me

config.itemsIntro: Three quick ground-rule checks to seal the badge:

items.stem: A classmate is upset by something she's seen online. What do you do?
options: Tell a teacher or trusted adult straight away
Screenshot it and share it around
Tell her to log off and forget it

items.stem: Your C2k login belongs to…
options: Just you — no one else, ever

items.stem: Something strange pops up on your screen. What's the agent move?
options: Ask the teacher before touching anything
Click it quickly to make it go away
Turn the monitor off and say nothing

config.intro: Time to learn your way around Mission Control itself. Follow the beacon — it will light up each part of your console.

stops.title: The Mission Board
stops.text: Seventeen operations. This is your whole year at a glance — every lesson you'll ever do in DT lives on this board.

stops.title: Locked & Unlocked
stops.text: A padlock means 'not yet' — your teacher unlocks each operation when it's time. Finished ones stay open forever, so you can always go back.

stops.title: Your Agent File
stops.text: Your badges, your XP, your progress ring. This is private — only you and your teacher can see it. No public scoreboards here.

stops.title: The Help Beacon
stops.text: Stuck? The beacon is always in the corner. It never gives you the answer — but it always gives you a way forward. And your teacher is beacon number two.

config.itemsIntro: Navigator check — three questions, then the badge is yours:

items.stem: Why do we take screen breaks and sit properly at a computer?
options: It protects your eyes and posture over long stretches
Screens stop working if you stare too long

items.stem: A lesson tile shows a padlock. What does that tell you?
options: Your teacher hasn't unlocked it yet

items.stem: You finish a lesson. Next fortnight, can you still open it?
options: Yes — completed operations stay open forever
No — lessons lock again behind you
Only if the teacher re-unlocks it

config.intro: Six files have landed in your Inbox. File each one where it truly belongs. Choose wrong and the Vault returns it — no hints, no answers. Reason it out from the labels.
config.pairPrompt: Work as a PAIR on this one: agree together before you release each file. Say your reason out loud — 'it goes there because…' — then drop.

debrief.sync: Freeze. Look at what just happened: you and your partner worked on the SAME thing at the SAME time, agreeing before every move. That's working together, live — computing's fancy name for it is SYNCHRONOUS (say: SINK-ron-us, 'at the same time').
debrief.async: But your Drive doesn't need anyone else there. You can open it alone, hours later, from ANY device — even at home. Working on a shared thing in your own time has a fancy name too: ASYNCHRONOUS ('NOT at the same time'). You'll use both all year.

config.intro: The Vault you just filed was a simulation. Time to stand in the real one.

steps.title: Open your real Drive
steps.text: Open a NEW tab and go to drive.google.com — on a school computer it signs you in by itself. That page is YOUR real Vault: it follows your login to any device, even at home.
steps.confirm: I can see my Google Drive

steps.title: Spot the + New button
steps.text: Top-left: the + New button. That's how folders get made. Next mission you'll build your real folder system right there — School, DT Work, the lot. For now, just know where it lives.

config.intro: Every agent's file opens with a baseline scan — sixteen questions about the digital world as you find it TODAY. This is not a test you can fail: it simply seals your Agent File so future-you can see how far you've come. Answer on your own, no conferring. Each answer is logged, not marked.

items.stem: Which of these is a piece of HARDWARE?
What does 'logging in' actually do?
options: Proves who you are so the computer opens YOUR account
Connects the school to the internet

items.stem: Which part of a computer keeps your files safe when the power is off?
A printer is an example of an…
Which of these connects a laptop to the internet WITHOUT a cable?
A website offers a free prize if you type in your home address. What should you do?
options: Don't enter it — and check with a trusted adult first
Enter it quickly before the prize runs out
Only give it to the website's chat helper

items.stem: Which of these is the strongest password?
A stranger in an online game asks which school you go to. Best response?
options: Don't say — and tell a trusted adult if they keep asking
Tell them — it's just being friendly
Ask which school THEY go to first

items.stem: You need a piece of work you saved last week. Where do you look?
Which key gives you a CAPITAL letter while you hold it down?
To COPY something you've selected, you press…

A robot is making toast. Its instructions so far:
1) Plug in the toaster
2) ???
3) Press the lever down
What is the missing step 2?
What comes next in the pattern? 2, 4, 6, 8, …
A friend follows your instructions EXACTLY and still gets the wrong result. The most likely reason?
options: Your instructions missed a step or weren't exact enough

items.stem: What IS the internet, mainly?
options: Millions of computers connected together, sharing information

items.stem: Your best friend asks for your C2k password 'just to check something'. What do you do?
options: Never share it — passwords are only for you
Give it to her — she's your best friend
Write it on a note so you're not saying it out loud
Change it to something she already knows

config.intro: Your Agent File is sealed. One thing remains: choose your codename and take the oath.
oath: I look after my own login, and only mine.
I save my work where it can follow me.
I ask for help when I'm stuck — and help others when they are.
If I miss a mission, I catch it up before our next one.
I am patient with myself while I learn.

belonging.title: A message from Mission Command
lines: Before you go — one thing every new agent needs to hear.

In your first weeks here, some things will feel hard. Logins will fail. Code will break. Files will hide. That is not a sign you're bad at this — it's what learning technology feels like for EVERYONE, including every agent who came before you and every adult in this building.
The feeling is normal, and it is temporary. Agents who keep going find that the thing that felt impossible in September feels easy by June.
You belong in this room, you belong in this subject, and your Agent File is open.

config.intro: One final scenario before you clock off, Agent.

items.stem: It's Friday evening. You want to show your family the work you finished in school today. Where did it need to be saved for you to open it AT HOME?
options: In my Google Drive — it follows my login on any device, anywhere
On the school computer I was using
It's impossible — school work can only be seen in school
On any school computer, as long as I remember which room

statements: I can log into my C2k account and find my saved work.
I can explain what a locked lesson tile means.
I know one way to make a strong password.
